clue.text: Small ball with which to shoot pool

parts.note: the jack is the small target ball in bowls
to pot is to shoot, as a hunter pots game

explanation.surface: A billiards player picks out the little ball to sink in a game of pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pool' reads as the table game, but it is the prize fund that builds up until someone wins it.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackpot is an accumulated pool of prize money, as in a lottery or card game.

clue.text: Servant woman tempted to crack timeless joke

indicators.note: to crack means the woman's name is put inside to split the other word
timeless means the letter for time, T, is dropped

parts.note: a jest is a joke
Eve is the woman tempted by the serpent in Eden

explanation.surface: A maid tempted to break into an old jest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woman tempted' looks like description, but it names the Eden figure; 'timeless' drops T and 'to crack' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeeves is P. G. Wodehouse's famous valet, the archetypal gentleman's gentleman.

clue.text: Bachelor in future fulfilling groom's role?

indicators.note: in means the bachelor's letter goes inside

parts.note: coming, as in the coming year, means future

explanation.surface: A bachelor in future taking on the role of bridegroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' looks like a bridegroom, which suits 'Bachelor'; it means to tidy hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Grooming hair is done with a comb, so passing one through is what a groomer does.

clue.text: Temple's role for females performing

definitions.note: the definition with 's for 'is': temple is

parts.note: a part is a role in a play
hen is used for women, as in a hen party
on means performing, on stage

explanation.surface: A temple's part for women acting in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'females' gives HEN as in a hen party, the British name for a women-only pre-wedding party.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parthenon is the temple of Athena on the Acropolis in Athens.

clue.text: Creature with bits protruding from foot to ear

definitions.text: Creature with bits protruding from foot to ear

parts.words: Creature with bits protruding from foot to ear
parts.note: an amphibian covered in warty lumps all over its body, from its feet to its head

explanation.surface: A monster studded with growths from head to toe.
explanation.definitionFit: Toads are famously warty amphibians, their skin covered in bumps from feet to head.

clue.text: For parents who are absent minded

definitions.text: For parents who are absent minded

parts.words: For parents who are absent minded
parts.note: read 'minded' as looked after children: for parents who were out, someone minded the little ones

explanation.surface: A remark about forgetful mothers and fathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absent minded' looks like the single word for forgetful; split it, and the parents are absent while someone else minded their children.
explanation.definitionFit: To have looked after someone's children while the parents were out is the past tense of a childcare verb.

clue.text: Treble 4 thrown, securing game

indicators.note: thrown means the letters are tossed into disorder

parts.note: the answer to 4 down, the warty creature

explanation.surface: A dart thrown at treble four wins the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treble' suggests darts scoring; with the 4-down answer it is fodder, and 'securing' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Battledore and shuttlecock is an old game, an ancestor of badminton.

clue.text: Opening barmaid's case, I agree, was a howler

indicators.note: opening means the agreement splits the case apart
case means the outside letters of the word, its casing

parts.note: aye is yes, I agree

explanation.surface: A barmaid's cover blown, I admit, was a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'howler' looks like a gaffe; it is a dog that howled. The first and last letters of 'barmaid' are B and D.
explanation.definitionFit: A hound that bayed gave a deep howl, so it was a howler.

clue.text: Reserves fuel -— it's found under the bed

parts.note: subs are substitutes, reserve players
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Spare players' fuel stashed beneath the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' suggests a bedroom; it is the topsoil bed of a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsoil is the layer of earth beneath the topsoil, the bed in which plants grow.

clue.text: Persuade to do lecture that's no good

indicators.note: that's no means the letter for good is missing

parts.note: a talking-to is a lecture, a telling-off

explanation.surface: Get someone to give a talk that's worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's no' removes G from TALKING TO.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk someone into something is to persuade them to do it.

clue.text: Film about end of war moved men greatly

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the single letter taken from war
moved signals that the letters of men greatly are shifted into a new order
end of picks out the final letter of war

explanation.surface: A war film's ending stirred its male audience deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' scrambles MEN GREATLY into ELMEGANTRY; 'about' wraps that round R, the last letter of 'war', giving ELMER GANTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmer Gantry is the 1960 Burt Lancaster picture adapted from Sinclair Lewis's novel about a fraudulent preacher.

clue.text: Unit of volume that starts apocryphal work

definitions.meaning: a unit of loudness, ten decibels, named after Alexander Graham Bell
the opening word of ... and the Dragon, a book of the Apocrypha

explanation.surface: A measure of space that opens a book of doubtful authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' suggests capacity or a book, but here it means loudness.
explanation.definitionFit: The bel measures sound intensity, and Bel and the Dragon is an addition to Daniel in the Apocrypha.

clue.text: Prophet in purdah silently returning

indicators.note: returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A holy man comes back quietly into seclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the hidden run AHSILE across 'purdah silently'; 'returning' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Elisha was the Old Testament seer who succeeded Elijah, so he is a biblical prophet.

clue.text: Some of Iris's family welcome in, only if restricted to odd visits

parts.note: glad, as in a glad welcome, means welcome as an adjective

indicators.note: restricted to odd means only the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of these words are kept

explanation.surface: Someone relatives of Iris are glad to have round, as long as they come only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iris' looks like a woman; it is the flower genus. 'restricted to odd' keeps letters 1, 3, 5 and 7 of 'in only if'; 'visits' merely finishes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladioli belong to the iris family, Iridaceae, so they are some of that family's plants.

clue.text: Old farmer reportedly cheers on arrest of very, very young thugs

indicators.note: arrest of means the farmer holds the two letters

parts.note: a Boer is a Dutch-descended farmer of South Africa, the word meaning farmer
V again for very
V again for very

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, not as written

parts.note: buoys, as in buoys up, means cheers

explanation.surface: An old farmer is said to applaud the arrest of very young hooligans.
explanation.walkthrough: BOVVER BOYS are British slang for skinhead-era yobs looking for 'bovver', Cockney for trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Bovver boys were young British hooligans of the 1970s, gangs of thugs spoiling for a fight.

clue.text: Guy's planning tea, then bed

parts.note: gunpowder is a Chinese green tea rolled into small pellets
a plot is a small piece of ground, such as a flower bed

explanation.surface: A man's arrangements: tea first, then off to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' is Guy Fawkes, whose 1605 plan to blow up Parliament is remembered in Britain on Bonfire Night.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1605 conspiracy was the scheme in which Guy Fawkes took part, so it was his planning.

clue.text: New soprano — it's alternative piper?

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the word it, with 's as the link 'is'

explanation.surface: A new soprano: it's another singer of pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piper' suggests a musician; it is the Pied Piper, who cleared Hamelin of rats.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pied Piper got rid of rats; rodent poison is another way to do that job.

clue.text: Current times stop Tracy having bottom pinched — that's a bit dated

indicators.note: stop means the two letters plug the gap inside the name
having bottom pinched means the last letter is taken away

parts.note: Spencer Tracy, the Hollywood actor
I is the symbol for electric current
X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: Tracy is pinched on the bottom, which now seems a bit old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: SPENCER loses its R; IX goes inside. A sixpence was an old British coin, and 'bit' is used for a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixpence was a pre-decimal British coin, so it is a piece of money now out of date.

clue.text: Drunkards produce Gospel in Latin

parts.note: the Latin proverb that people in their cups speak the honest truth, the 'gospel' they utter

explanation.surface: Tipplers turn out a scripture translated into Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gospel' suggests a book of the Bible, but here it means plain truth, which the Latin saying claims drinkers let slip.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'in wine, truth': drinkers blurt out what is true.

clue.text: Were clearing banks so secure?

definitions.meaning: leapt over, as a horse clears fences
kept in strongrooms, as a bank keeps valuables safe

explanation.surface: Banks were secure while clearing cheques.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clearing banks' suggests the British high-street banks that clear cheques; split it into two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaulted means jumped over, and also stored in a vault.

clue.text: Humping something that's picked up on his advice?

definitions.text: Humping something that's picked up on his advice?

parts.words: Humping something that's picked up on his advice?
parts.note: a specialist in lovemaking, whose advice teaches the act

explanation.surface: A removals man explains how to lift heavy objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humping' looks like carrying a load; it is slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular blend for a specialist adviser on sex, a sex expert.

clue.text: Chap informally the cause of planes crashing?

definitions.meaning: an informal word for a man or bloke
one who fells trees, here plane trees

explanation.surface: A bloke who brings aircraft down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planes' suggests aircraft, but they are plane trees, brought down by a woodcutter.
explanation.definitionFit: Feller is a casual word for fellow, and also one who fells timber.

clue.text: Sacks quietly left beneath spades

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
under means beneath
S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Bags placed softly to the left, underneath the garden tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacks' reads as bags; it is the verb, to loot. 'beneath' is no positional instruction but gives its own synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to pillage it, the same as stealing goods by force.

clue.text: Belief a tiny dose one too big to be knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means the whole run is read backwards, as a drink is knocked back

parts.note: mg, milligram, is a tiny dose
OD is an overdose, a dose too big

explanation.surface: A conviction that a small dose is one too many to swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be knocked back' turns A MG OD into DOGMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogma is a firmly held belief or doctrine.

clue.text: Winger from team breaking metatarsal, say

indicators.note: breaking means the team's letters split the bone open

parts.note: a metatarsal is one example of a bone, in the foot
XI, eleven, is a football or cricket team

explanation.surface: A football wide man from the side fractures a foot bone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls footballers' broken metatarsals; 'Winger' is a bird, not a wide player.
explanation.definitionFit: The bonxie is the Shetland name for the great skua, a seabird and so a winged creature.

clue.text: Strike stone, causing end of obelisk to drop off

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of obelisk

parts.note: to nap is to drop off to sleep

explanation.surface: Hitting a stone column makes its tip fall off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop off' suggests falling; it means to doze.
explanation.definitionFit: To knap is to strike and shape flint or stone, as in flint-knapping.

clue.text: Matthew and the rest going around university in the buff

indicators.note: going around means the testament letters surround the university letter

parts.note: Matthew and the other gospels and epistles make up the New Testament, NT

explanation.surface: The gospel writers jog round the campus naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the buff' reads as naked; split it, and 'buff' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A buff is an enthusiast, and so is a nut, as in a film nut.

clue.text: Forming opinion school's OK

parts.note: read as schools: to ground a pupil is to school them in basics
well means OK, in good health

explanation.surface: A pupil forms a view that the school is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school's' looks like a noun with an apostrophe, but it is the verb, 'schools', meaning grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A groundswell is a build-up of public feeling, opinion gathering strength before it breaks.

clue.text: Turned up as reformed characters do, losing face

indicators.note: losing face means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: reformed characters mend their ways

explanation.surface: Former rogues turn up having lost all dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing face' takes M off the front of MEND WAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed endways stands on its end, upright, so it is turned up.

clue.text: Joker ludicrously sent up queen

indicators.note: ludicrously signals that the letters of sent up are jumbled absurdly

parts.note: R, regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A comic absurdly lampooned the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' reads as mocked, but it is the fodder, which 'ludicrously' rearranges before the queen's letter is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A punster is a person who makes wordplay jokes, a joker of a particular kind.
